feedback: Written before this robot has raced, so no outcome is stated. There is no earlier race telemetry yet. My integration choices so far are only the contract-based defaults. The controller uses a modest kp (4) and small ki and kd, because the 0.05 m lead and 10 mm pitch have not been tested and I do not want to hide sensing problems with aggressive gains. Nothing has been compensated for yet. Next race, decide as follows. If line_loss_events is high or rms_error rises on the S-bend and slalom, the sensors are probably losing the tape between samples, so widen the footprint or the pitch (see requested change 1). If steering_oscillation is high while line_loss_events is low, the lead is too long for the gains, so move the sensors closer to the axle (change 2). If completion_time is above about 3 s or the robot slips in bends, the drivetrain is the limit, so reduce mass or widen the track (change 3).
requested_changes: If line_loss_events is more than about 2 on the development tracks, try sensor_size 0.016 with the same five positions. This widens the footprint so the outer sensors keep a graded signal across the 25 mm tape edge.
If steering_oscillation is high with few line losses, try sensor y = 0.03 instead of 0.05 for all five sensors. This reduces the lead time that causes phase lag at the current gains.
If completion is 0 or completion_time is over about 2.7 s, try wheel_track 0.10 and mass 0.6. This should make turns quicker and reduce slip, at the cost of less stability on fast bends.
